title: Batch gate: align workspace dependency features so per-crate prebuilds do not recompile lower crates

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

body:
`gate batch` runs one `cargo test -p <crate> --no-run` prebuild for each crate (`#2727`) so later per-crate suite steps reuse the exact feature resolution.

In `batch-20261121-112020/0[1-9]-debug_build_*.log`, per-crate feature divergence caused repeated recompilation inside one warm batch run:
- `01-debug_build_geometry`: compiled `kernel`, `geometry` (6 s).
- `02-debug_build_kernel`: compiled `kernel` with `truck` dev-feature (4 s, expected).
- `05-debug_build_post`: recompiled `kernel`, `geometry`, `cl`, and `post` (15.7 s).
- `08-debug_build_app`: recompiled 6 third-party crates (`ring`, `rustls`, `reqwest`, ...) plus `kernel`, `geometry`, `cl`, `tools`, `post`, `sim`, `motion`, and `app` (169 s).
- `09-debug_build_ui`: recompiled 10 third-party crates (`spade`, `tracing-subscriber`, `num`, `solidcore-tess`, `reqwest`, ...) plus `kernel` through `app` and `ui` (58.9 s).

One batch run compiled `kernel` 5 times, `geometry` and `cl` 4 times, `tools`/`post`/`sim`/`motion` 3 times, and `app` 2 times. This adds ~40–60 s to every warm batch run and multiplies unit variants in `target/debug/build/`.

Identify the diverging optional dependency features across `crates/*/Cargo.toml` (using `cargo tree -e features`) and align the workspace dependency feature declarations so `geometry`, `cl`, `tools`, `post`, `sim`, `motion`, `app`, and `ui` share one compiled rlib per lower crate during `gate batch`.

Evidence and measurements: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/919#issuecomment-7065686766

Done means: in a warm `cargo xtask gate batch` run, each workspace library crate (`geometry` through `app`) compiles once across the 9 prebuild steps (only `kernel` repeats for its `truck` dev-feature), verified from the `01..09` build logs.

Part of #919
